newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen lower on good supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen lower on good supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were seen slipping further on Friday to fresh low this week on heavy supplies, traders said.
Weak bunker demand and high stocks were also putting further pressure on prices, traders said.
While some chinese demand were heard to have emerged, traders said current supplies were more than sufficient to meet demand.
A trader said a 20,000 tonne cargo of 180-cst supplies were sold by a South Korean trader for delivery to south China at the end of January at $6.50 per tonne premia c+f over Singapore spot quotes.
Another 30,000 tonne cargo was heard to have been sold at $7.50-$8 per tonne premia c+f basis, also for end January delivery to south China from Japan.
Cash prices for end January loading supplies were quoted at $120-$122 per tonne on Thursday.
Late Thursday, an offer was seen at $118 per tonne from a major for end January loading.
In the swaps market, front-month January was last quoted at $116.50/$1117.50 per tonne, down from Thursday's quotes at $119/$120.
